newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Indices rise on Ivory Coast bourse.
newsitem.headline: Indices rise on Ivory Coast bourse.

text.p: Indices on Ivory Coast's stock exchange, the Bourse des Valeurs d'Abidjan (BVA), rose in the week to Friday in a session marked by a capital increase by a leading bank, its market report showed.

The BVA All-Share Index rose 1.32 percent to 363.72 points from 358.99 points, taking the 1996 rise to 31.19 percent. The 12VB 12-share index rose 0.03 percent to 246.67 points from 246.60 points, taking the 1996 rise to 23.79 percent.
Bank SOGBCI fell 3,810 CFA francs to 11,840 CFA francs after giving away one new share for three already held as part of a capital increase.

But cement company SOCIMAT-CI (+500 CFA to 28,500 CFA), transit company SICM (+200 to 29,840 CFA), ELF OIL-CI (+990 CFA to 20,840 CFA) and motor finance company SAFCA (+100 CFA to 51,870 CFA) all rose.
Volume was 38,189,000 CFA, down from 150,077,000 CFA the previous week. Just 1,367 shares were traded against 6,446 the previous week.
The BVA index stood at 277.25 points at the end of 1995, the 12VB at 199.26 points.
The Abidjan bourse recorded a 78.57 percent rise in market capitalisation to 400 billion CFA in 1995.
